\# Hosting a GitHub Page - R Cheat Sheet

# Story Pitch Rough Draft

## Summary of Pitch

Donald Trump’s first presidency introduced an increase in defense contracting that came at the expense of domestic programs, while former President Biden claimed that he would not decrease defense spending during his time in office, according to a 2022 Guardian article. 

But under the Biden administration, Lockheed Martin — the defense contractor that was awarded the most money from the government in 2020 and 2024 —  received 25.6 billion less dollars. 

In my story, I would like to track the difference in defense contract spending within the Trump and Biden administration. 

## Modern day Relevance

Although there is largely centrist bipartisan support for defense spending, it would be interesting to see how each president interacted with defense companies. I would want to look into the CEOs of each company and who they decided to throw their support behind in the 2020 and then the 2024 election. This could explain Trump's current interaction with defense contracting.

## Target Audience

I would likely be targeting an audience that is interested either positively or negatively about decreases in defense spending. 

## People I would interview

1.  Ryan Bradel - He is a partner at the Ward and Berry, a D.C law firm that specializes in government contracting. He's represented multiple defense contracting, and so he would be able to give an expert opinion on how to navigate the information.
2.  Reach out to press contacts for the defense contracting that I am covering so that they have a chance for comment on the amount of government spending they receive.
3.  I would reach out to the DOW, and Pete Hegseth's team for comment on how the department allocates spending towards contractors.

## Potential impact

Because I am going to look at where the funding for the defense contractors are going to be allocated by state and county, I will be able to see the impact that defense contractors have in local communities. Beyond the bipartisan separation on defense spending, it would also be interesting to see if there would be any impacts on jobs when defense spending is cut.

## Interesting aspects of the story

Although I have had limited time with the data I pulled, I was already able to see the differences in spending between the Trump and Biden administration. I think that the fact that multiple child corporations of Lockheed Martin show up in the top ten highest obligations indicates that there are only a couple of defense contractors that hold a large amount of power in the US. I also thought it was interesting that one of the only contractors that received more money under the Biden administration was the organization dedicated to defense healthcare. This shows a difference in priorities between the two administrations.

## Previous coverage

I noticed that a lot of the previous coverage of the story compared the similarity in spending between the final year of the Trump administration and the first year of the Biden administration. I think that it would be also interesting to cover the difference between 2020 and 2021, but also 2021 and 2024 to see if Biden evolved on his defense spending throughout his tenure in office.

## Visuals

I am planning on looking at each defense company over each year of the presidency, so I will be doing a line chart for those. I also plan on doing a bar chart which lists the amount of money given to each defense company. When I do a state analysis I plan on creating a map.

## More information

I still need to complete my state and county analysis, and deeper analysis on each contractor. If I was trying to see if there were lifestyle changes in the counties with increases or decreases in funding, I would look at GDP data by county/state to see if there were any differences.

Creating an API key that can pull the defense contractors and amount in 2020

```{r}
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)


body <- list(
  filters = list(
    time_period = list(
      list(
        start_date = "2019-10-01",
        end_date   = "2020-09-30"
      )
    ),
    agencies = list(
      list(
        type = "awarding",
        tier = "toptier",
        name = "Department of Defense"
      )
    )
  ),
  limit = 10,
  page = 1
)

response <- POST(
  "https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_category/recipient/",
  body = body,
  encode = "json"
)

data <- fromJSON(
  content(response, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"),
  flatten = TRUE
)

top10_2020 <- data$results %>%
  select(
    contractor = name,
    uei,
    obligations = amount
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(obligations))

print(top10_2020)
#Both parent and children corporations were showing up in these results - which I think could still be accurate because they both receive funding. My main concern is just making sure that they are not repeating the amounts. 
#Lockheed Martin received 39,981,831,442 in 2020, and that does not include the child corporation amount
```
Doing the same thing again for 2024
```{r}
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)


body <- list(
  filters = list(
    time_period = list(
      list(
        start_date = "2023-10-01",
        end_date   = "2024-09-30"
      )
    ),
    agencies = list(
      list(
        type = "awarding",
        tier = "toptier",
        name = "Department of Defense"
      )
    )
  ),
  limit = 10,
  page = 1
)

response <- POST(
  "https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_category/recipient/",
  body = body,
  encode = "json"
)

data <- fromJSON(
  content(response, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"),
  flatten = TRUE
)

top10_2024 <- data$results %>%
  select(
    contractor = name,
    uei,
    obligations = amount
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(obligations))

print(top10_2024)
#Both parent and children corporations were showing up in these results - which I think could still be accurate because they both receive funding. My main concern is just making sure that they are not repeating the amounts. 
#Lockheed Martin received 14,357,199,730 - less than half of what they received under the Trump administration 
#Boeing Company was up higher, but still received less money; Humana recieved more money - but that is also the health care for the military 
```

## Set up for hosting

-   Create a new folder in your repository called "docs" (if one isn't there already)
-   Rename this document as "index.qmd"
-   Move "index.qmd" into the "docs" folder

## Render this document as an html page

-   Make sure this document is named "index.qmd" and is in the "docs" folder
-   Click Render button. It will create an html version of this page, called "index.html"
-   Use GitHub Desktop to push your files to your your github repository on the web.
-   Access the URL from your Github repository.

## Host html on GitHub

-   Go to your github repository on the web, such as https://github.com/djnf-data-2026/casey-mann
-   Click on Settings on the top right.
-   Scroll down to the Pages section of Settings.
-   Change the Branch to /docs and click save.

#### To see your file hosted:

-   Back to your GitHub repo on the web: such as https://github.com/djnf-data-2026/casey-mann
-   Click on Settings, then Pages
-   Under GitHub Pages, you should see "Your site is live at https://djnf-data-2026.github.io/casey-mann/"
-   Click that URL
-   If it works, email it to robwells\@umd.edu
